column2: Today's pre-work safety check starts at 7:30 a.m. in front of Plant 1.
On the scaffold, always clip your harness lanyard to the horizontal lifeline before moving.
Do not remove the opening cover on the 2nd floor; if you do remove it, put it back immediately after the work.
In aisles where forklifts pass, walk only inside the pedestrian lane.
We identified three hazards in today's TBM: falls, pinch points, and electric shock.
If you do not tighten the chin strap, your hard hat will come off your head in a fall.
Keep flammable materials out of a 5-meter radius around welding work.
Before entering a confined space, measure the oxygen level and confirm it is 18 percent or higher.
Appoint only one crane signaler, and follow that person's signals only.
If you feel unwell during work, do not endure it; tell your team leader right away.
Working across the guardrail of an aerial work platform means an immediate work stoppage.
Before using a power tool, run your hand along the cable to check for stripped insulation.
Keep the distribution panel door closed and locked; when it must be opened, call the electrical supervisor.
Lay scaffold boards at least two deep and keep gaps under 3 centimeters.
Do ladder work in pairs, with one person holding the ladder from below.
Never run a grinder with the wheel guard removed.
On steel beams both hands must be free, so always hoist materials with a rope.
The area around the sump pit on basement level 2 is slippery, so wear rubber boots when you go in.
If a fire starts, shout to warn others first, press the emergency bell, and then evacuate.
The assembly point is the safe zone in the main gate parking lot, and the team leader counts heads.
Pull the safety pin on the extinguisher, squeeze the handle, and aim at the base of the fire.
5 minutes of stretching before work greatly reduces back injuries.
Do not lift materials over 20 kilograms alone; split the load between two people.
When lifting something heavy, bend your knees, keep your back straight, and hold it close to your body.
Do not wear cotton gloves when using a cutter, because the gloves can be caught by the blade.
Near rotating machinery, always tuck in sleeves and straps so they stay against your body.
Wear earplugs in areas where the noise level exceeds 85 decibels.
Do not cover the warning label on a hazardous chemical container, and keep the lid firmly closed.
In areas where thinner is used, turn on the ventilation fan and keep the door open.
Write the date of first use on the respirator cartridge and replace it once the period has passed.
When repairing a machine, cut the power and attach a lock so that no one else can switch it on.
The person doing the repair keeps that lock's key in their own pocket.
Do not reach into a conveyor just because it has stopped; always confirm the power is isolated.
A press requires both hands on the two-hand buttons, so never tape one button down.
Riding on forklift forks is forbidden in every case.
Do not stack loads above eye level, and keep heavier items at the bottom.
If a pallet is cracked, do not use it; collect it separately in the disposal area.
Materials left in an aisle block escape routes in an emergency, so clear them right after work.
If oil spills on the floor, spread absorbent immediately and put up a warning sign.
Do not run on the stairs, hold the handrail, and do not climb with materials in both hands.
Do not put a utility knife in your pocket with the blade out.
Today's temperature is above 33 degrees, so we rest 10 minutes in the shade every hour.
Drink a cup of water every 20 minutes, and taking it with salt is even better.
Dizziness or a headache is an early sign of heat illness, so tell us immediately.
In winter, spread sand on icy stretches and check for slipperiness before work.
If it rains, stop steel and scaffold work and switch to indoor tasks.
Stop tower crane work when the wind speed exceeds 10 meters per second.
Welding sparks fly up to 10 meters, so lay spark blankets on the floor below.
After work, hang the tools in their places, count them, and report the number to your team leader.
If you find an injured person, first prevent a second accident and then call 119.
The first aid kit is on the wall to the left of the office entrance, and the defibrillator is next to it.
For bleeding, press with a clean cloth and raise the wound above the level of the heart.
If a chemical gets in your eyes, rinse with running water for at least 15 minutes.
Do not pull an electrocuted person with bare hands; cut the power first.
If an accident happens during work, record it without fail, however small it is.
Confirm today's training with your signature, and we will take questions after the session.
If Korean is difficult, please raise your hand. We will explain again through interpretation.
The most frequent accident at this site is slips and falls, and the next is pinch injuries.
Hot work cannot start without a work permit.
Before high-risk work, the work supervisor stays on site with you until the end.
In 2-person work, if your partner leaves the spot, stop work and wait.
Do not walk while looking at your phone, and take calls in the safe zone.
You cannot come to work after drinking, and if you have taken medication, tell us in advance.
Smoking outside the designated area carries a very high fire risk.
Safety training for foreign workers becomes a legal requirement on January 8, 2027.
Today's session is 50 minutes with a 10-minute break in the middle.
Before work, check your own five pieces of protective equipment yourself.
If the soles of your safety shoes are worn, apply for a replacement rather than keep wearing them.
Wear safety glasses underneath the welding mask as well.
Do not sweep metal filings from cutting work with bare hands; use a broom.
Do not walk under an overhead crane; go around it.
Before work, inspect lifting gear and wire rope for broken strands.
If broken strands exceed 10 percent in one lay of a wire rope, do not use it.
If a hoist remote button sticks while pressed, cut the power immediately and report it.
Tools left on a work platform fall and injure the people below.
Tie tools used at height to your wrist or harness with a lanyard.
Cap the ends of rebar to prevent puncture injuries.
Pull the nails out of timber right away and collect them in one place.
When work ends, shut off the electricity and gas, and the team leader checks last.
Tomorrow we have scaffold dismantling work, so we will practice two-lanyard hook-up.
Hello. I am your guide for today. Please put the earphone in your left ear.
The gate you see now is Gwanghwamun, the main gate of Gyeongbokgung Palace.
Geunjeongjeon is where the Joseon royal court held its largest ceremonies.
The broad flat stones on the ground are called bakseok, and they reduce glare from the sun.
Gyeonghoeru is a pavilion built over an artificial pond, and it is especially beautiful in spring.
Take your photos here and gather under this pine tree in 10 minutes.
The restroom is 30 meters along the wall on your right.
The stairs are narrow, so please go up slowly in a single line.
Keeping about two steps from the person ahead will keep you from tripping.
People still live in Bukchon Hanok Village, so you must walk quietly.
The inner alleys are private property, so please take photos only from the street.
We will have lunch at 1 p.m. and meet again here at 2 p.m.
At Gwangjang Market, the most famous dishes are mung bean pancake and mayak gimbap.
Some shops take cash only, so please have about 10,000 won (1 man won) ready.
If you are worried about spicy food, I will ask the shop to make it milder.
The bus is parked in front of Exit 3, and its number is 1234.
If you leave your bags on the bus, take only your valuables with you.
The ride takes 40 minutes, so feel free to rest.
The wind is strong at Seongsan Ilchulbong in Jeju, so it is better to carry your hat.
There are 580 steps to the top, and the round trip takes 50 minutes.
If your knees bother you, going only as far as the middle viewpoint is fine.
At Bulguksa Temple, we do not take photographs inside the main hall.
Some places require taking off your shoes, so wearing socks is a good idea.
The full wall trail of Hwaseong Fortress in Suwon is 5.7 kilometers around.
Today we will walk only 1.5 kilometers of it.
You can rent a bicycle on Nami Island, and it costs 10,000 won per hour.
The last boat leaving the island is at 6:40 p.m.
If you lose the group, call my number and wait where you are.
Keep your passport in an inner pocket of your bag and do not carry it in your hand.
Pickpockets are rare, but in crowded markets please wear your bag in front of you.
This museum is closed on Mondays, and today it is open until 6 p.m.
In the exhibition rooms, please stay one step back from the artworks.
This is a room where photography is allowed if you turn off the flash.
This piece is 12th-century Goryeo celadon, and its blue-green bisaek color is its hallmark.
If you look at the number under an artifact, you can find its description in the exhibition booklet.
This painting was done on silk and fades easily, so the lighting is kept dim.
The room you see now is on the 2nd floor, and the next talk will be in the sculpture hall on the 3rd.
The elevator is behind the information desk, and a wheelchair fits inside.
The special exhibition runs only until the 15th of next month, and after that you cannot see it.
Drinks may be had only in the lounge outside the exhibition rooms.
If your bag is large, please put it in a locker at the entrance, and do not lose the key.
Today's talk is 40 minutes, and I will take questions at the end.
If you can hear my voice clearly, please raise your hand once.
If the sound cuts out, the text keeps appearing on your screen, so you can read that instead.
These subtitles appear in the language you chose, while I speak only Korean.
There is no shade once we go out to the outdoor site, so you will need a parasol or a hat.
The ground on the fortress wall is uneven, so I recommend sneakers.
When it rains the stone paving is very slippery, so please hold the handrail.
The hanok village talk is given while walking, so please stay within three steps behind me.
Group photos come out best in front of these stairs.
The gift shop is next to the exit, and a postcard is 2,000 won.
You do not need to return the earphone to me after the tour. It is yours.
We walked about 4 kilometers today, roughly 20,000 steps.
The next item is a 7 p.m. performance, and our seats are in the middle of the second floor.
Please switch your phone to silent inside the theater.
I would be grateful if each of you shared a word at the end about today's tour.
Tomorrow we leave from the hotel lobby at 8:30 a.m.
It will get colder, so please bring one more layer.
You may ask questions now, or ask while we walk.
Thank you for joining us today. I hope you travel home safely.
All right, let's begin. Today we start with Chapter 3, reading financial statements.
Let me sum up the income statement we covered last time in one sentence.
Please open your textbook to page 47. We will look at Table 3-2 together.
In this table the horizontal axis is the quarter and the vertical axis is revenue.
The unit is millions of won, so think of 6 zeros after each number.
This concept will definitely appear on the midterm, so be sure to write it down.
If I am going too fast, please raise your hand. I will say it again.
If Korean is difficult, it helps to follow the subtitles on your screen.
I will also say the English term for technical words: gamgasanggak, depreciation.
The assignment is due by next Tuesday, and late work loses 10 percent.
Keep the assignment under 2,000 characters and cite at least three references.
Copying someone else's text is plagiarism and will be graded 0.
When you quote, put the author and the year in parentheses as the source.
Group projects are in teams of four, and we will form the teams next session.
Each team presents for 8 minutes, plus 2 minutes of questions, for 10 minutes total.
Keep your slides to ten pages and make the text nice and large.
I will take attendance by QR code at the end of class today.
Three absences mean an F under school rules, so please keep that in mind.
If you cannot come because you are ill, let me know by email in advance.
The exam has 20 multiple-choice questions and 2 written questions.
You may bring a calculator, but a phone cannot be on your desk.
I will print the formulas on the first page of the exam. You do not have to memorize them.
But you do have to know where to apply them in order to solve the problems.
Let's work through this problem together. First we organize the given values.
If revenue is 12 billion won and costs are 9.5 billion, operating profit is 2.5 billion.
As a ratio, the operating margin is about 20.8 percent.
Here we will keep only two decimal places.
If you do not write out the steps, you will not get full credit even with the right answer.
In this graph, the slope means the speed of change.
The point where the graph bends is called the inflection point.
That is enough theory; let's look at one case.
Look at how this indicator moved during the 2008 financial crisis.
At that time unemployment rose from 3.2 percent to 4.0 percent within a year.
Do not memorize the numbers; remember the direction and the reason.
Let me summarize today in three sentences.
First, a financial statement is less a photograph of a company than a video.
Second, cash flow is the number to read before profit.
Third, a ratio means nothing on its own and only gains meaning in comparison.
Any questions? If not, we take 10 minutes and start the second hour.
During the break, read practice problems 1 through 5 at the back of the textbook.
Let's resume. I will check whether the back rows can hear me well.
If the microphone is too quiet, tell me and I will turn it up a little.
If the writing on the board is too small, you may take a photo.
I will upload the class materials to the learning management system this evening.
Let me explain the two mistakes that came up most in the last assignment.
One was leaving out the units, and the other was omitting the source.
Next time we cover Chapter 4, cost calculation, so please read it beforehand.
If you mark the parts that are hard to read, I will explain those first.
My office is room 305 on the third floor of the engineering building, and office hours are Wednesdays from 2 to 4 p.m.
When you email me, please put the course name and your student number in the subject line.
Use today's recording for review only and do not post it anywhere.
This course is 30 percent midterm, 40 percent final, 20 percent assignments, and 10 percent attendance.
Grade appeals are accepted only within 3 days of the announcement.
International students can get assignment feedback at the Korean writing support center.
The center is on the 2nd floor of the library, and you book it on its website.
If you get nervous while presenting, speak slowly. That is better than speaking fast.
You do not have to answer my question right away. Taking 1 minute to think is fine.
Today's lecture notes will remain on your phone after class ends.
Those notes contain both my original words and the translation in your language.
That is all for today. Thank you for your work.
